title: Conjecture 2 (Alon [2])
statement_text: Let $G$ be a group of size $n$. The independence number of the random Cayley graph $G(p)$ is at most $\tilde{O}(p^{-1})$ whp.
context_text: It is natural to conjecture that random Cayley graphs behave similarly to random regular graphs of the same degree in terms of independence number. The best prior general bound was $O(\min(p^{-2}(\log n)^{2}, \sqrt{n(\log n)/p}))$ (Theorem 1). The conjecture is significantly harder to approach than its random-regular-graph analogue due to limited randomness and strong dependencies in the Cayley graph model.
paper_contribution: Proves improved bounds on the independence number of sparse random Cayley and Cayley-sum graphs, making progress toward the conjectured $\tilde{O}(p^{-1})$ bound; a companion follow-up work achieves sharp asymptotics for $G=\mathbb{Z}_n$ at density $(\log n)^{-2+o(1)}$.
notes: Reference [2] is: N. Alon, 'The chromatic number of random Cayley graphs', European J. Combin. 34 (2013), 1232–1243.
paper_title: Random Cayley graphs and random sumsets

title: Conjecture 15
statement_text: Let $G$ be an abelian group of order $n$ and let $s\le n$. There exist collections $\mathcal{F}_{\ell}$ of subsets of $G$ such that $\log|\mathcal{F}_\ell|=\tilde{O}(2^{\ell})$ and $\min_{F\in\mathcal{F}_\ell}|F|=\tilde{\Omega}(2^{\ell}s)$, and such that for every $A\subseteq G$ with $|A|=s$ and $|A+A|\leq K|A|$, there exists $\ell\leq\log_{2}K$ and $F\in\mathcal{F}_{\ell}$ such that $A+A\supseteq F$.
context_text: $A+A=\{a+b: a,b\in A\}$ is the sumset, $|A+A|\le K|A|$ means that $A$ has doubling at most $K$, and $\tilde{O},\tilde{\Omega}$ hide polylogarithmic factors in $n$. The authors' main covering lemma proves this with weaker parameters: there are $C,c>0$ and collections $\mathcal{F}_\ell$ with $|\mathcal{F}_\ell|\le\exp\left(C\min\left(2^{2\ell}(\log n)^2,\sqrt{2^\ell s(\log n)^{3/2}}\right)\right)$ and $\min_{F\in\mathcal{F}_\ell}|F|\ge c2^\ell s/\ell^2$ with the same covering property; in particular, it answers Lovett's question by giving a collection of $\exp(O((\log n)^2))$ sets of size at least $\epsilon n$ such that $A+A$ contains one of them whenever $|A|\ge\delta n$. The motivation is graph-theoretic: in the random Cayley graph $G(p)$ (vertex set $G$, $x\sim y$ iff $y-x\in S$, where each pair $\{x,-x\}$ is put in $S$ independently with probability $p$) and the random Cayley sum graph $G^+(p)$ ($x\sim y$ iff $x+y\in S$, each element in $S$ with probability $p$), a set $A$ is independent in $G^+(p)$ exactly when $A+A$ avoids $S$, so the collections $\mathcal{F}_\ell$ act as a union-bound cover: $G^+(p)$ has no independent set of size $s$ whp if $\sum_\ell\sum_{F\in\mathcal{F}_\ell}(1-p)^{|F|}=o(1)$. With the covering lemma the authors show that the independence numbers of $G(p)$ and $G^+(p)$ are $\tilde{O}(p^{-3/2})$ whp for abelian $G$ and $p\le 1/2$, the first improvement on the exponent $p^{-2}$; the conjectured optimal cover would characterize the independence number of sparse random Cayley graphs up to logarithmic factors, in line with Alon's conjecture that it is $\tilde{O}(p^{-1})$ whp.
